newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic sees pacemaker, ICD market growth.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic sees pacemaker, ICD market growth.

text.p: Medtronic Inc expects to maintain a nearly 50 percent share of the world pacemaker market, which it sees expanding to about $2.5 billion in annual sales this fiscal year from about $2.4 billion last year, said chief financial officer Robert Ryan Tuesday.

The medical devices maker estimated the world market for implantable defibrillators was $750 million in the fiscal year ended April 30, of which Medtronic commanded a share in the high 40 percent range, Ryan said in a presentation to investors attending a Piper Jaffray conference.
The implantable defibrillator, or ICD, market is projected to grow to about $1 billion this calendar year, said Piper Jaffray analyst Arch Smith.
A pacemaker is an electronic device implanted in the body and wired to the heart to keep it from beating too slowly; an implantable defibrillator is similar, but regulates a too rapid heartbeat.
Medtronic leads the competitive world markets for both devices, which last year accounted for roughly two-thirds of company revenues.

Numerous new product launches in these and other categories are planned for this fiscal year, with the greatest resulting boost to profits expected in the second half of the year, Ryan said in remarks to investors.
The company's new line of Kappa pacemakers is expected to be launched in the United States in the second fiscal quarter, which begins August 1.
Clinical testing of its new Gem ICD series should start in th next two fiscal quarters, with commercial launch still some months away.
U.S. Food and Drug Administration marketing approval for Medtronic's Wiktor stent is expected.
"The Wiktor should be approved shortly," Ryan said.

European commercial release is anticipated later this calendar year for the company's Aneurx AAA stented graft, which is designed to make abdominal aortic grafting surgeries much less traumatic and cheaper.
The Freestyle porcine-tissue heart valve is expected to clear the FDA before the end of the second fiscal quarter, Ryan said.
Finally, the Activa device for controlling essential tremor and tremor related to Parkinson's Disease is expected to hit the market this fiscal year, as well, Ryan said.
